currentContext.business: MBL specialises in executing civil engineering projects across highways (EPC, BOT and O&M), housing, urban infrastructure, railways/metro, and other infrastructure, primarily for public-sector clients such as NHAI, MoRTH, State PWDs, DMRC and state road development corporations. The Company was among the first contractors awarded and to complete the NHAI North-South-East-West Corridor and was among the earliest entrusted with National Highway maintenance. Having exited a period of financial restructuring under an approved IBC Resolution Plan, MBL is now transitioning from highway EPC concentration towards a diversified infrastructure platform spanning steel plant modernisation, industrial infrastructure, irrigation, power transmission and public health engineering.

currentContext.strengths: Over three decades of execution experience in civil engineering and infrastructure project delivery|Among the first contractors awarded, and the first to complete, NHAI's North-South-East-West Corridor programme; one of the initial contractors entrusted with National Highway maintenance by NHAI|Established client relationships with NHAI, MoRTH, State PWDs, DMRC, MPRDCL and BSRDCL|Track record of modernisation and civil works for SAIL/Durgapur Steel Plant, petrochemical infrastructure and Commonwealth Games-related infrastructure, providing a base for diversification into adjacent sectors|Long-standing regional presence and relationships in West Bengal/Kolkata, seen as a competitive advantage as eastern India infrastructure investment picks up|Reinstated regular banking facilities and renewed lender confidence following completion of the Resolution Plan, restoring working-capital access for bidding and execution|Disciplined, selective bidding strategy that avoided commercially unsustainable pricing during a period of intense competitive margin compression in the highway EPC sector
currentContext.strategies: Disciplined, selective bidding: the Company chose not to match irrational/aggressive bids during a period of industry-wide margin compression, preserving financial stability and prioritising sustainable returns over headline topline growth.|Diversify from a business predominantly built around highway EPC contracting towards a broader infrastructure platform — Steel Plant modernisation, civil engineering, Urban Infrastructure, Public Health Engineering, Irrigation Infrastructure, Electrical Transmission, Industrial Infrastructure, Commonwealth Games (Ahmedabad)-linked works — built on existing engineering credentials rather than unfamiliar terrain, to broaden the revenue base and reduce single-segment dependence.|Strengthen the Quarrying, Concrete, Bitumen, and Construction material & tolling divisions.|Complete the remaining subsidiary resolution process as a foremost strategic priority for FY2026-27.|Leverage long-standing corporate presence and execution experience in West Bengal/Kolkata to capture growing industrial and infrastructure development opportunities across eastern India.|Draw upon strengthened banking relationships, improved liquidity and enhanced financial flexibility to participate in larger and more complex infrastructure opportunities.|Anchor future expansion on a robust financial platform rather than excessive leverage; maintain disciplined capital allocation and prioritise long-term shareholder value creation over aggressive revenue expansion or market share pursuit.
currentContext.expansion: MBL frames its next phase as a shift from resolution/recovery to renewed project execution rather than a specific capacity build-out: implementation of its IBC Resolution Plan has cleared debt and restored operational liquidity and institutional credibility, and the Company has resumed bidding for new infrastructure projects. Growth is expected to come from diversifying beyond highway EPC into new verticals — Steel Plant modernisation, civil engineering, Urban Infrastructure, Public Health Engineering, Irrigation Infrastructure, Electrical Transmission, Industrial Infrastructure, and Commonwealth Games (Ahmedabad)-linked developments — alongside strengthening its existing Quarrying, Concrete, Bitumen, Construction material & tolling divisions. Six of the Company's eight subsidiaries have been cleaned up and rendered debt-free; the Resolution Plan for the remaining subsidiary, Suratgarh Bikaner Toll Road Company Private Limited, has been submitted to lenders and is expected to be resolved during FY2026-27.
currentContext.mdna: India's infrastructure sector is witnessing robust demand driven by integrated planning, higher investment and technology-led execution, positioning the country for sustainable economic growth and scalable infrastructure development.|Government capex-led growth: Union Budget 2026-27 allocation to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways of H3,09,875 crore, an 8% increase over the FY2025-26 revised estimate, with NHAI set to receive H1,87,293 crore of that allocation.|The road infrastructure sector is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9-10% over the next several years, outpacing the broader construction industry, backed by H19.5 lakh crore proposed for construction/widening of ~41,000 km of roads by 2031-32 and ~USD 80 billion of monetisation pipelines being executed through InvITs and toll auctions.|Structural, durable demand drivers: urbanisation, population growth, rising freight volumes, and the drive to reduce India's logistics costs from 13-14% of GDP towards globally competitive levels.|Evolving contracting structures (Hybrid Annuity Model, Toll-Operate-Transfer, InvIT) are de-risking developer participation and unlocking institutional capital; over 75% of new road development is now expected to flow through PPP models.|Bharatmala Pariyojana, PM GatiShakti and Vision 2047 together provide a decade-long pipeline visibility that supports private-developer investment in equipment, talent and capacity.|The highway EPC sector's preceding three years of aggressive, commercially unsustainable bidding and margin compression is expected to give way to more disciplined industry bidding behaviour.|Indian economy outlook remains resilient, driven by strong domestic consumption and investment with medium-term growth potential of around 7%, though rupee depreciation and import-cost inflation (fuel, fertilisers) and global trade-policy uncertainty are flagged as headwinds.|Future order acquisition would be guided not by volume alone, but by the ambition to build a diversified and genuinely high-quality order book, with project selection prioritising commercial viability, execution capability, risk profile and long-term profitability.|For FY2026-27 and beyond, the Company aims to secure new orders while building a genuinely diversified portfolio spanning highways, industrial infrastructure, civil engineering, irrigation, power transmission and other infrastructure, with diversification expected to improve revenue visibility even as it reduces concentration risk.

risks.note: A significant portion of the current order book is concentrated in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, exposing the Company to region-specific economic, administrative and execution-related risks.
Delays in settlement of receivables, arbitration awards and contractual claims may affect liquidity, working capital availability and cash flow visibility.
Scheduled repayment obligations related to NCDs and ECBs could exert pressure on future cash flows if expected operating and recovery inflows are delayed.

Inability to secure or execute large projects within specified timelines could lead to project delays and tied-up funds; risk factors include challenging terrain, adverse weather, labour shortages, supply-chain disruptions, cost escalations and force majeure events.
The Company's historically limited business strategy (concentration in highway EPC) could impact its ability to capitalise on opportunities in a growing, diversifying infrastructure market.

Increased competition from established contractors and financially strengthened industry participants, including a rising number of mid-sized entrants, may impact project acquisition opportunities and bidding margins.
Lower-than-expected traffic volumes, toll collection fluctuations or operational disruptions could affect returns from the Company's BOT assets and concession operations.

Changes in government policies, project-awarding mechanisms, EPC contract structures, concession frameworks or infrastructure spending priorities may influence business opportunities and project economics.
